title: The grammar clinic: 15 mistakes
prompt: Sam wrote this short essay about a four-day school week but didn’t edit it. It has 15 grammar mistakes: verbs that don’t agree, wrong tenses, pronouns, there/their and its/it’s, comma splices, a fragment, capitals and a missing comma. Fix all 15 right in the writing box. The checklist counts each fix and explains it.
starter:
Every student in our school know how tiring a five-day week can be. Some schools in the United States has already switched to a four-day week, and many families like it. A four-day week would give students more rest, more family time and more time for there hobbies.

First, a longer weekend gives students time to rest. Tired students cannot focus, they make more mistakes in class. When students is rested, they learn faster. Because sleep helps the brain store new ideas.

In addition families would have more time together. My cousin and me visit our grandparents every saturday, but we always have to leave early. With a three-day weekend, families could take short trips or relax at home, the school would also save money on buses and electricity. Last year, the bus company raises its prices twice.

Some people argue that a four-day week would leave younger children without care. However, schools could offer a club day on fridays for families who needs it. Each school would choose it’s own plan.

A four-day week would help students rest, learn and enjoy there families. Our school board should try it for one year and see the results.
tips: Edit in passes: verbs first, then pronouns and word choice, then sentences, then capitals and commas.
Read each sentence alone: does it make sense by itself?
Stuck? Use the hint button in the checklist.

errors.explanation: “Every student” is singular, so the verb is “knows”.
errors.hint: First sentence: does the verb match “every student”?

errors.explanation: The subject is “Some schools” (plural), so the verb is “have”.
“Their” shows belonging; “there” is a place.
Two sentences joined by only a comma make a comma splice. Add “and” or “so”, or use a full stop.
errors.hint: Second paragraph: two sentences joined by a comma.

errors.explanation: “Students” is plural, so the verb is “are”.
“Because sleep helps…” can’t stand alone: join it to the sentence before.
errors.hint: Second paragraph: a sentence that starts with “Because”.

errors.explanation: Put a comma after an introductory phrase like “In addition”.
errors.hint: Third paragraph: the first two words.

errors.explanation: Take away “My cousin and”: “I visit”, not “me visit”.
Days of the week take capitals.
errors.hint: Third paragraph: a day of the week.

fixes: at home, and the school would
errors.explanation: Another comma splice: split it into two sentences or add “and”.
“Last year” is the past, so the verb is past tense: “raised”.
Days of the week take capitals.
“Families” is plural, so the verb is “need”.
“Its” shows belonging; “it’s” means “it is”.
“Their” shows belonging.

At this point in time, each and every student owns a tablet.
Because it rained, the game was cancelled.

title: Cut the extra words
prompt: This paragraph about recycling says too much with too many words. Find the 11 wordy phrases and replace each with a shorter one right in the writing box. The checklist counts each fix. Keep the meaning the same.
starter: In order to understand why recycling matters, it is important to note that most garbage ends up in landfills. Due to the fact that landfills are filling up, each and every town has the ability to make a difference. At this point in time, a large number of families already recycle on a daily basis. The reason why is because recycling saves energy and materials. In spite of the fact that sorting takes time, the end result is worth it.
tips: Look for phrases the Coach underlines as wordy.
Ask: can one word do the same job?
Stuck? Use the hint button in the checklist.

errors.explanation: “To” says the same as “in order to”.

errors.wrong: matters, it is important to note that most
errors.explanation: “It is important to note that” adds nothing: start with the point.

errors.wrong: Due to the fact that landfills
errors.explanation: “Because” replaces “due to the fact that”.
“Each and every” says the same thing twice.
“Can” replaces “has the ability to”.
“Now” or “Today” replaces “at this point in time”.
“Many” replaces “a large number of”.
“Daily” replaces “on a daily basis”.

errors.wrong: The reason why is because recycling
errors.explanation: “The reason why is because” says “because” three times.

errors.wrong: In spite of the fact that sorting
errors.explanation: “Although” replaces “in spite of the fact that”.
A result is already the end.

title: The writing process
instructions: Put the steps of writing an essay in order.

items.text: Choose a prompt and decide your position or focus.
Plan with an outline: thesis, body points, evidence, conclusion.
Draft every paragraph without stopping to fix small things.
Revise: fix the structure, evidence and explanations.
Edit: grammar, punctuation, formal words.
Read it aloud one last time, then submit.

explanation: Big changes first (revise), small changes last (edit).

title: Review Jordan’s essay
prompt: Practise self-review on someone else’s writing first. Jordan’s introduction and first body paragraph have 12 problems: informal words, contractions, wordy phrases, vague words, “I think” and grammar. Fix all 12 right in the writing box. The checklist counts each fix.
starter:
Have you ever tried to learn something hard? I think that learning to swim is a really good thing for kids. Swimming is a life skill that keep people safe in the water. Every child should learn to swim because it builds confidence, keeps them healthy and could save a life.

First, swimming builds confidence. When kids learns to float, they stop being scared of the water. My little brother was terrified of pools, but after ten lessons on saturdays he jumped off the diving board. Due to the fact that he could swim, he felt brave enough to try a lot of new stuff. Now he doesn’t want to leave the pool, he asks to go every weekend. It’s clear that a skill like swimming has the ability to make children believe in themselves. In my opinion, every school should offer lessons.

Write contractions out in full.
